title: Ultrastructural Characterization and Sexual Dimorphism in Antennal Sensilla of Hyblaea puera (Lepidoptera: Hyblaeidae), A Pest of Mangrove and Teak
content:
Abstract
Hyblaea puera (Cramer) (Lepidoptera: Hyblaeidae) is a destructive pest of teak and mangrove ecosystems worldwide. To better understand the chemical communication between this insect and its host plants, we examined the morphology, ultrastructure, and distribution of antennal sensilla in both sexes using scanning and transmission electron microscopy. Seven sensillum types were identified: sensilla trichodea, sensilla chaetica, sensilla basiconica, sensilla squamiformia, sensilla styloconica, sensilla coeloconica, and böhm sensilla. Sensilla trichodea were the most abundant, followed by basiconica and coeloconica. The number of sensilla per flagellomere did not differ significantly between the sexes across the three flagellar sections. Sexual dimorphism in the antennae of H. puera is manifested as variations in sensillum size, with the most pronounced differences observed in sensilla trichodea, basiconica, and coeloconica, all of which are longer in females than in males. Transmission electron microscopy further revealed the internal structure of sensilla trichodea, basiconica, squamiformia, and sensilla coeloconica. The putative functions of the antennal sensilla types are discussed in relation to the structural features. We expect these results to help understand the chemosensory mechanisms in H. puera and facilitate the development of pheromone-based management tools.
